b: Thomas Nagel is the 2026 winner of the $1 million Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture.

The Berggruen Institute called Nagel, professor emeritus of philosophy and law at New York University, “one of the most significant philosophers of our time,” and praising his “long-lasting contributions through his scholarly work and commentary in the public sphere,” referencing his work in moral philosophy, legal and political theory, metaphysics, and philosophy of mind, and his contributions to our understanding of consciousness, existence, altruism, equality, justice, and free will.

In a press release, Nicolas Berggruen, the chairman and founder of the Berggruen Institute, says, “The Institute is pleased to recognize Thomas Nagel for his interrogation of the human experience and for expanding consciousness and our capacity to understand ourselves.”

The Berggruen Prize, according to the Institute, “seeks to place philosophical thought of the highest caliber on center stage of the public discourse and to amplify its significance to society.” It was created in 2016 and is awarded annually.
